setup: The equation sets the absolute value of a trigonometric function equal to a positive constant, and the interval covers [[N]] periods of that function.

steps.say: An absolute value equation splits into two signed equations, one for the positive value and one for the negative value.
Each period of the function holds the same number of solutions for each sign, because the graph repeats exactly.
Multiplying the count in one period by the [[N]] periods covers the interval, and the two signs occur at different angles so no solution is counted twice.
